1.word_for_word: aṣṭāviṃśe — in the twenty-eighth chapter; tataḥ nanda-ānayanam — then the bringing back of Nanda; varuṇa-ālayāt — from Varuṇa's abode; vaikuṇṭha-darśanam ca — and the vision of Vaikuṇṭha; gopānām anuvārṇyate — is described for the cowherds; govardhanam samuddhṛtya — having lifted Govardhana; vaśe kṛtvā amareśvaram — having brought the lord of the gods, Indra, under control; nanda-ānayanataḥ — by recovering Nanda; varuṇam ca vaśe anayata — Kṛṣṇa also brought Varuṇa under submission
1.translation: In the twenty-eighth chapter, the recovery of Nanda from Varuṇa's abode and the cowherds' vision of Vaikuṇṭha are described. Having already lifted Govardhana and brought Indra, lord of the gods, to submission, Kṛṣṇa now, by retrieving Nanda, also brought Varuṇa under his authority.

2.word_for_word: kalā-mātrāyām dvādaśyām — when only a small portion of Dvādaśī remained; pāraṇa-ādara-abhiniveśena — because of intense concern to complete the fast properly; āsurīm velām avijñāya — not recognizing the inauspicious demonic period; aruṇa-udayāt pūrvam — before dawn; śāstra-balena niśi udakam praviṣṭam — entering the water at night on the strength of a scriptural rule; tat anabhijñaḥ varuṇasya bhṛtyaḥ anayad — Varuṇa's servant, not understanding the religious reason, took him away; aḍhajanatā māmakena — ‘by my servant acting unknowingly’; bhagavad-dharmam ajānatā — ignorant of the Lord's dharma
2.translation: Only a small portion of Dvādaśī remained, and Nanda was intent on performing the prescribed breaking of the fast at the proper time. Not realizing that the moment before dawn was an inauspicious interval for bathing, he entered the water at night on the authority of a scriptural rule concerning such a short Dvādaśī. Varuṇa's servant did not understand Nanda's religious purpose and carried him away. This is why Varuṇa later says, ‘my servant did it unknowingly’—that is, without understanding the Bhagavata religious observance involved.

3.word_for_word: svānām — to his own people; bhagavad-dharma-parāṇām — devoted to the Lord's dharma; abhaya-daḥ — giver of fearlessness; mā bhaiṣṭa iti — saying ‘do not fear’; abhayam dadat — granting reassurance
3.translation: Kṛṣṇa, the giver of fearlessness to his own people who are devoted to the Lord's dharma, reassured them: ‘Do not be afraid.’

4.word_for_word: sa-paryayā arhaṇena — with ceremonial worship and due honor
4.translation: Varuṇa received Kṛṣṇa with full ceremonial worship and appropriate honors.

5.word_for_word: adya idānīm me dehaḥ nibhṛtaḥ dhṛtaḥ — only today has this body of mine truly been sustained; yadā tvat-darśanam jātam — when the sight of you occurred; tadā eva deha-sāphalyam prāptam — only then did embodiment attain its purpose; yad vā nibhṛtaḥ pūrṇa-manorathaḥ — alternatively, nibhṛta means my desire is fully satisfied; adya eva arthaḥ adhigataḥ — only today has true wealth/meaning been obtained; sarva-ratnākara-patinā — by me, lord of the ocean, repository of all jewels; pūrvam na evam-vidhaḥ arthaḥ prāptaḥ — never before was such a treasure obtained; saṃsāraḥ api nivṛttaḥ — saṃsāra itself is now ended; tvat-pāda-bhājaḥ — for those who serve your feet; adhvanaḥ pāram — the far shore of the road, liberation
5.translation: Varuṇa says: ‘Only today has my body truly fulfilled its purpose, because today I have seen you.’ Alternatively, ‘nibhṛta’ means that his deepest desire has now been completely fulfilled. ‘Only today have I gained real wealth’: though he is lord of the ocean, the repository of all jewels, he has never obtained a treasure like this before. He further implies that saṃsāra itself is now ended, for those who serve Kṛṣṇa's feet reach the far shore of the journey—liberation.

6.word_for_word: bhagavate — to Bhagavān, possessing unsurpassed sovereignty; brahmaṇe — to Brahman, the complete; paramātmane — to the Paramātman, controller of all living beings; na yatra — where not; loka-sṛṣṭim vikalpayati yā māyā — māyā that projects the creation of worlds; sā yatra na śrūyate — there it is not truly operative; avidyamānā iva tiṣṭhati — it remains as though nonexistent
6.translation: Varuṇa bows to him as Bhagavān, possessed of unsurpassed sovereignty; as Brahman, the complete reality; and as Paramātman, the ruler of all beings. The reason is that in him the māyā that projects the worlds has no binding operation; relative to his own nature it stands as though nonexistent.

7.word_for_word: ajānatā mad-bhṛtyena — by my servant acting unknowingly; tvat-pitṛ-āharaṇam — the taking away of your father; yat kṛtam — what was done
7.translation: ‘What was done’ refers to the fact that Varuṇa's servant, acting without understanding, seized Kṛṣṇa's father.

8.word_for_word: nandam vimucya — releasing Nanda; samarpayati — Varuṇa hands him back; govinda iti — with the address ‘O Govinda’
8.translation: Varuṇa releases Nanda and formally returns him to Kṛṣṇa, addressing the Lord as ‘Govinda.’

10.word_for_word: atīndriyam — beyond ordinary sense experience; adṛṣṭa-pūrvam — never seen before; loka-pālasya mahodayam aiśvaryam — the extraordinary magnificence and sovereignty of the guardian of the world
10.translation: Nanda had witnessed the extraordinary, previously unseen majesty of Varuṇa, a world-protector—an experience beyond anything ordinarily available to the senses.

11.word_for_word: autsukya-yuktā dhīḥ yeṣām — whose minds were filled with eagerness; api kim sva-gatim sva-sthānam — perhaps our own ultimate destination and proper abode; sūkṣmām brahma-ākhyām ca — subtle and known as Brahman; upādhāsyati — will he grant/show it; naḥ asmān prāpayiṣyati — will he bring us there; iti saṅkalpitavantaḥ — this is what they began to hope
11.translation: The cowherds became intensely curious. Their thought was: ‘Will Kṛṣṇa perhaps reveal to us, or bring us to, his own ultimate abode—subtle, transcendent and associated with Brahman?’

12.word_for_word: svānām teṣām saṅkalpam — that wish of his own people; akhila-dṛk sarva-jñaḥ — the all-seeing, omniscient Lord; svayam eva vijñāya — knowing it directly himself; teṣām saṅkalpa-siddhaye — to fulfill their intention; kṛpayā — out of compassion; etat vakṣyamāṇam acintayat — conceived the act described next
12.translation: The all-seeing, omniscient Lord directly knew the unspoken desire of his own people. Out of compassion and in order to fulfill it, he resolved upon what is described next.

13.word_for_word: avidyā — ignorance; deha-ādi-aham-buddhiḥ — the identification ‘I am the body’ and similar notions; tataḥ kāmaḥ — from that comes desire; tataḥ karma — from desire comes action; taiḥ ucca-avacāsu — by these one wanders through higher and lower births; deva-tiryag-ādiṣu — among gods, animals and other forms; bhraman — wandering; svīyām gatim na veda — one does not know one's own true destination
13.translation: Ignorance consists in identification with body and the like. From that comes desire, and from desire action. Driven by these, a being wanders through higher and lower births—divine, animal and otherwise—and no longer knows its own true destination.

14.word_for_word: svam brahma-svarūpam — his own Brahman-nature; lokam vaikuṇṭha-ākhyam ca — and the realm called Vaikuṇṭha; tamasaḥ prakṛteḥ param — beyond darkness, beyond material prakṛti
14.translation: Kṛṣṇa intended to show both his own transcendent Brahman nature and his realm called Vaikuṇṭha, which lies beyond the darkness of material prakṛti.

15.word_for_word: deha-ādi-pihitānām darśanam aśakyam — for those covered by bodily identification, direct vision is impossible; prathamam deha-ādi-vyatiriktam brahma-svarūpam darśayām āsa — first he revealed Brahman as distinct from body and other coverings; satyam — real, never sublated; jñānam — consciousness, non-inert; anantam — infinite, unlimited; jyotiḥ — self-luminous light; sanātanam — eternal; śaśvat-siddham — eternally accomplished; guṇa-apāye guṇa-apohe jñāninaḥ yat paśyanti — what knowers behold when the guṇas have fallen away; tat kṛpayā eva darśayām āsa — he showed that only by grace
15.translation: Because those covered by bodily identification cannot directly perceive the transcendent realm, Kṛṣṇa first revealed the nature of Brahman as distinct from body and all such coverings. ‘Satyam’ means reality that is never sublated; ‘jñānam,’ consciousness rather than inert matter; ‘anantam,’ the unlimited; ‘jyotiḥ,’ self-luminous; ‘sanātanam,’ eternal and ever-accomplished. This is what knowers perceive when the material guṇas are removed, and the cowherds saw it solely through Kṛṣṇa's grace.

16.word_for_word: brahma-hradam — the lake of Brahman; brahma eva hradavat hradaḥ — Brahman itself conceived like a lake; tatra nimagnasya viśeṣa-vijñāna-abhāvāt — because one immersed in it has no differentiated cognition; tam brahma-hradam te nītāḥ — they were brought to that Brahman-lake; tasmin magnāḥ ca — and immersed in it; punaḥ kṛṣṇena uddhṛtāḥ — then raised out again by Kṛṣṇa; samādheḥ iva utthāpitāḥ — like being brought out of samādhi; brahmaṇaḥ tasya eva lokam vaikuṇṭha-ākhyam dadṛśuḥ — they then saw the realm of that same Brahman called Vaikuṇṭha; yatra kṛṣṇe nimitte sati pūrvam akrūraḥ adhyagāt — by Kṛṣṇa's agency Akrūra too had formerly beheld it; atarkya-aiśvarye bhagavati kiñcit api asambhāvitam na — nothing is impossible for Bhagavān of inconceivable majesty; athavā — alternatively; akrūraḥ yatra dṛṣṭavān tasya yamunā-hradasya brahma-hrada iti nāma — the Yamunā pool in which Akrūra had his vision may itself be called Brahma-hrada; tam hradam nītāḥ — they were taken to that pool; brahmaṇaḥ lokam dadṛśuḥ — and there saw Brahman's realm
16.translation: Śrīdhara offers two readings. On the first, ‘Brahma-hrada,’ the ‘lake of Brahman,’ is Brahman itself metaphorically conceived as a vast pool. Immersed in it, the cowherds temporarily had no differentiated cognition. Kṛṣṇa then raised them out as one awakens from samādhi, and they beheld the manifest realm of that very Brahman, Vaikuṇṭha. Akrūra had likewise obtained such a vision through Kṛṣṇa; nothing is impossible for Bhagavān's inconceivable power. Alternatively, ‘Brahma-hrada’ may be the name of the Yamunā pool in which Akrūra had previously received his vision. On this reading Kṛṣṇa took the cowherds to that pool; there they saw the realm of Brahman, and afterward he brought them out again, leaving them astonished.
